title: Paloma and the Harvest
premise: Silas Ashgrove, a hospice nurse who dismisses the backwards-counting she hears from the dying, takes a post at Marrow House, a decommissioned sanatorium whose grounds are being excavated for a vineyard. The crew unearths a cellar door sealed from the inside, and the last living resident, ninety-year-old Ada Voss, begins signing away the estate — papers that will legally bury what happened in 1974, when six patients vanished. Silas discovers the dead are counting down to the harvest, when the vineyard's first pressing would seal the door forever, and that Ada was the one who locked it, with the six inside. To end it, Silas must open the door, return what was taken — Ada's stolen confession, hidden in a nurse's locket — and let the dying finish their count aloud. In the end, Ada signs nothing; she walks down into the dark to join those she sealed away, and Silas, finally believing, hears silence instead of numbers.
about_author: Casper Joubert is the pen name of a former hospice orderly from the Karoo who spent eleven years listening to the last words of the dying. He writes horror about the debts families refuse to acknowledge, and claims he has never once counted backwards himself.

chapters.title: The Backwards Count
chapters.summary: Silas arrives at Marrow House to care for Ada Voss, whose lucid days are numbered. At night she counts backwards from numbers Silas doesn't give her — 74, 73, 72. The excavation crew strikes a stone door sealed from the inside, and the counting in the ward grows louder. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: professional detachment beginning to crack.

chapters.title: What Ada Kept
chapters.summary: Silas finds a nurse's locket in the sealed cellar's antechamber, containing a 1974 confession naming Ada as the one who locked six patients below during an 'infection control' order. Ada, lucid for one terrible hour, begs Silas to burn it — then begs her to read it. POV: Silas, with Ada's spoken testimony. Emotional beat: horror of complicity; justice and mercy at war.

chapters.title: The Last Pressing
chapters.summary: The vineyard's owners accelerate the harvest to press before the estate dispute resolves, and the counting reaches single digits. The dead manifest in the ward — six shapes counting in unison, Ada among them in the visions though she still breathes. Silas realizes the door opens only for the one who sealed it, or the one who carries what was taken. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: dread tipping into resolve.

chapters.title: Zero
chapters.summary: On harvest night, Silas carries the locket down and opens the door from the outside. Ada descends to face the six, confessing aloud what the papers would have buried, and the counting stops at one — hers. She signs nothing; she signs herself over. The dead finish their count and go quiet. Silas stays on as Marrow House's last nurse, listening to silence. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: grief, restitution, and the terrible peace of finally believing.
